steps.note: One step. It records the ask; the amount and the recovery schedule are approved together by somebody else, because an advance approved without a schedule is a loan nobody agreed the terms of (BR-2).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A zero amount, a missing reason and an advance already outstanding all arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the request and the audit entry together or not at all. No money moves and nothing is deducted. The schedule proposed here is a proposal — what is actually deducted is agreed at approval, before the money reaches the employee (BR-3).

An employee holds one advance at a time unless the school permits more, so recovery does not stack beyond what a salary can carry (BR-9).

planningRules.rule: Never supply the amount. It is what the employee needs, and a figure derived from their salary is a planner deciding how much of somebody's pay to commit for months.
Never compose the reason. It is what the approver weighs (E3), and a reason written for an employee is the school deciding what their circumstances were.
Never approve in the same plan. The request and the approval are separate acts by separate people, and an employee approving their own is refused outright (BR-1, E5).

Report an existing outstanding advance rather than treating it as a formality. An employee holds one at a time so recovery does not stack beyond what a salary can carry (BR-9), and the second ask usually means the first is still being repaid.

Say plainly that the schedule is only proposed. What is deducted each month is agreed at approval, before the money arrives (BR-3), and an employee who assumes their proposal stands will be surprised by the first payslip.

reversal.statement: An advance is never deleted. A request that is not granted is rejected with a reason, and both stay on the record (BR-12).
